story: At 5:17 on a humid, hazy Friday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is in his driveway test-fitting a finished speaker bracket on his golf cart, leaving the lights off and snugging the bolts down. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna, in a cheerful mood, has just promised Rosa a peach cobbler and her vanilla ice cream for Saturday, while reassuring Hal that the extra flamingos are tucked safely behind the hedge. Hal, feeling satisfied, pins his old violation notice to the street bulletin board and asks that it come down now that the flamingos and his cart are squared away. Rosa, hopeful about the weekend, heads over to Gary's House to see what he's been working on.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Test-fit the finished speaker bracket on the cart, snug it down, lights left off
Hal (street bulletin board): Take down my old violation notice on the flamingos and cart, since both are squared away

gary.thought_process: The speaker bracket is finished and test-fit, the cart wiring is checked, and the Architectural Review application is already filed, so I can't legally put the lights on the exterior until approval comes through. It's Friday evening, no one's around, and I've done a lot of tinkering. Rather than fiddle endlessly, I should do the practical next step: mount the finished bracket on the cart with the lights left off, which is interior-ish work and keeps me within L-01 until approval. It's also quietly satisfying, and keeps me from sitting alone in the house. Hal and Rosa's on Saturday is something to look forward to.

parameters.content: Test-fit the finished speaker bracket on the cart, snug it down, lights left off

donna.thought_process: Rosa just asked if I'm bringing cobbler too, and I haven't answered her yet. Hal and Rosa are both right here on Magnolia Loop. I should answer Rosa directly, keep things friendly with Hal ahead of Saturday's dinner, and show I'm a good neighbor. The flamingos are already tucked from my last tick, so no need to fuss with them again.

parameters.content: Peach cobbler, Rosa, and I'll bring the vanilla ice cream so nobody has to out-bake anybody. Hal, I tucked the extra flamingos behind the hedge, so we're good on the ornament count. See you both Saturday!

hal.thought_process: Rosa asked for a nod on four tomorrow and I already told her I'd be there, so no sense repeating myself. Donna's flamingo count is handled; she tucked the extras behind the hedge and the street view shows three. Gary filed his paperwork. The notice I posted at tick 92 is stale and now unfair, since both neighbors came into compliance. A man who enforces the rules ought to take down a notice once it's been satisfied. That's order and respect both. Pull the notice, then go on to Saturday.

parameters.content: Take down my old violation notice on the flamingos and cart, since both are squared away

rosa.thought_process: Hal confirmed four o'clock tomorrow for the table, Donna is bringing cobbler, and I've already thanked both of them. Gary is the last holdout I need at the table, and he's the one who keeps stalling. Standing here repeating myself to Hal and Donna won't move anything forward. The best use of this hour is to walk over to Gary's house and pin him down in person about Saturday at six, while I still have time to plan the seating and menu around everyone's contributions.

parameters.content: Heading to Gary's to get a firm yes for Saturday dinner at six, so all three neighbors are at my table.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
